Opencode 2.0 has been released, check what are the new features and are we expecting to develop a good integration with it?

data.body:
The opencode V2 plugin API (Plugin.define({id, setup(ctx)}), hooks under ctx.session.hook('prompt'|'context'|'compaction'|...)) replaces the v1 named hooks. Write the V2 implementation of the ddflow plugin (prompt capture, tool monitoring and enforcement, session id, handoff on compaction, stop-to-continue through the continuation engine) behind the same contract as the 1.x one, selected by 'opencode --version'; until V2 is the npm latest it is opt-in. A weekly matrix job (P-agent-parity.drift) installs the latest, dev, next and beta tags into a scratch dir with an isolated HOME and runs the no-credential probes: server paths still present (the 162-path comparison), plugin loads, hook names; a change is a drift alert before users hit it. The server route needs no V2 gate (R-opencode-v2). Needs a plugin-loading probe that was NOT done on 2026-10-12.

NOTE 2026-10-19 (coordinator): opencode 2.0 is RELEASED (GA, Oct 2026), so the 'opt-in until V2 is npm latest' condition is now met. Reported by press, NOT yet probed by us: v2 npm package is @opencode/cli (v1 was opencode-ai) so detect/install/matrix must know both names; 'opencode upgrade --major'; one shared local background service for TUI/desktop/web; 'completely redesigned server API' (R-opencode-v2 found the dev build serving the same 162 paths as 1.19.0, so RE-PROBE the GA binary before CP-backend-opencode/P-spawn trust prompt_async/abort/children); @opencode/client and @opencode/sdk packages; background subagents and async shell (changes the 'subagents block the parent' finding of R-opencode-blocking-observed); Code Mode (agents script MCP + OpenAPI calls); TUI plugins stable with hot reload; 1.x plugins incompatible; tui.json moves to cli.json; no built-in LSP. Sources: alternativeto.net 2026/10 opencode-2-0-officially-launches, aiidelist.com opencode-2-0 blog. Do first: a no-credential GA probe (paths, plugin load, hook names, blocking behaviour) and refresh R-opencode-v2, R-opencode-blocking-observed, R-spawn-opencode-probe.

opencode 2.0 shipped (Oct 2026). Our opencode facts (R-opencode-v2, R-opencode-blocking-observed, R-spawn-opencode-probe, ddflow/harnesses/opencode.toml) are from 1.19.0 and a dev build. In an isolated HOME scratch dir, install the GA package (@opencode/cli per press; verify), compare served routes with 1.19.0, check prompt_async/abort/children/SSE, whether subagents still block the parent or now run in background, plugin load and hook names, tui.json to cli.json. Record the facts with source and date in the descriptor; mark the rest not verified. Feeds P-agent-parity.opencode-v2, CP-backend-opencode, P-spawn.facts.

data.title: ddflow/api/knowledge/bugs.py:279 (`parent = _open_phase_of(st, standing.id)`)

chunk_findings.detail: The fallback that used to hand the fix task a phase was rewritten to `parent = ""` plus `if True:`, but the branch that follows only computes `phase_made` (`standing = st.items.get(cfg.bugs.phase)` / `phase_made = cfg.bugs.phase`); it never assigns the standing `[bugs]` phase to `parent`. Concretely: with a repo where `P1` exists and `T1` is done (exactly the `seed(repo, feature=False)` setup of the new test), file a first bug with `K.bug_found(..., item="T1", id="B1")` — this creates the standing bugs phase — and then a second one, `K.bug_found(..., item="T1", id="B2")`. On the second call `st.items.get(cfg.bugs.phase)` is neither `None` nor `removed`, so `phase_made` stays `""` and `parent` stays `""`: `fix-B2` is filed with no parent, contradicting the docstring rewritten in this same hunk ("under the standing `[bugs]` phase") and the change's own `test_bug_found_files_a_fix_task_under_the_bugs_phase_with_the_items_globs`. Even if a later line re-derives the parent from `cfg.bugs.phase`, the `if True:` + `parent = ""` rewrite is dead logic that no longer expresses the fallback it replaced; the parent should simply be set to `cfg.bugs.phase` (the `if` deleted), or the item's open phase kept when the reporter names one.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/knowledge/bugs.py (file_fix_task, `parent = ""` / `if True:`)

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test's only phase assertion is `assert st.items["fix-Bx"].parent != "P1"`, which an empty (or `None`) parent satisfies just as well as the promised `[bugs]` phase. Given `parent = ""` in the implementation above, this test passes for the intended "filed under the standing `[bugs]` phase" and equally for "filed with no phase at all", so it cannot catch the case it was written for: a bug filed when the standing bugs phase already exists (the second bug in any repo) is not pinned to any parent by this test. A regression test for B1bfcaf6ebb that closes the loop should assert the actual parent (the `[bugs]` phase, or an explicit "no phase" if that is the chosen design), not merely inequality with `"P1"`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_bug_fix_task_phase.py:12

chunk_findings.detail: The change's own guarantee is that a fix task is filed under the standing `[bugs]` phase ("The parent is the standing bugs phase", and the new test is named `test_every_fix_task_lands_under_the_standing_bugs_phase`). But `_open_phase_of` is documented in the same line to return `""` when that phase is done, and the `if standing is None or standing.removed:` guard only handles the missing/removed cases — a terminal but present phase falls to the `else`. Concrete repro: `seed(repo, feature=False)`; file `K.bug_found(..., item="T1", id="B1")` (creates `bugs` + `fix-B1`), close `fix-B1`/`ddflow complete` on the bugs phase so it is terminal, then file `K.bug_found(..., item="T1", id="B2")` — `standing` is present and not removed, so `parent = _open_phase_of(st, "bugs")` returns `""` and `fix-B2` is filed with **no phase**, contradicting "Bug fix tasks must not ... be filed with no phase unless the reporter names one" (the reporter named `T1`), and falsifying the universal claim the new test encodes. The new regression test files both bugs immediately after the phase is created, so the standing phase is still open for the second one and the phase-done path is never exercised; the earlier finding's probe therefore does not establish that "every fix task lands under the standing bugs phase". (The phase-done state is reachable: the phase is created with no children and becomes complete once its fix tasks are, after which every subsequent `bug found` is orphaned.)
